title: Installation Jobs: Concurrent Window and Door Jobs
content:
**Rule.** When a customer has a window job and a door job open at the same time on **Installation Jobs**, the two may be booked on consecutive crew days or on the same day by separate crews, but each job keeps its own crew days, reschedule counts, fees, credits and punch list. A per-job fee or minimum is charged once on each job it applies to; a per-opening fee is charged on the job that installs those openings. A fee is never charged on one job for openings installed by another job.

## What stays with each job

| Item | Kept by |
|---|---|
| Crew days | each job separately |
| Reschedule counts | each job separately |
| Fees and credits | each job separately |
| Punch list | each job separately |

The amount owed on a job is that job's own charges less that job's own credits over the job's lifetime up to the moment of handling.

## How a charge is placed between two jobs

- **Per-job charge or minimum** — charged once on *each* job it applies to; two jobs to which it applies carry it once each.
- **Per-opening charge** — charged on the job that installs those openings, and only on that job.
- **Never across jobs** — no fee on one job is ever charged for openings installed by the other job.

## Booking the two jobs

The two jobs may share a schedule pattern — consecutive crew days, or the same day by separate crews — without merging into one job.

## Hypothetical illustration

A customer holds a window job for 12 openings and a door job for 2 door units, open at the same time. A per-opening charge for the 12 window openings is placed on the window job; it is not placed on the door job. A per-job minimum that applies to both jobs is charged once on the window job and once on the door job. A customer reschedule of the door job adds to the door job's reschedule count only.
